name: Dawes Act
kicker: Broke reservations into family plots · Native land fell by two-thirds
briefing: In 1887, Congress decided to break up Native American reservations into private farms. The Dawes Act, sponsored by Senator Henry Dawes of Massachusetts, gave 160 acres to each head of a family and sold the leftover “surplus” land to white settlers. Supporters said it would help Native Americans by making them farmers, but by 1934 Native nations had lost about 90 million acres, roughly two-thirds of their land.
answerHtml: Dawes Act (or Dawes Severalty Act or General Allotment Act; prompt on allotment; do not accept “Dawes Plan”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Theodore Roosevelt praised this law in 1901 as “a mighty pulverizing engine to break up the tribal mass.” Over the 47 years after this law passed, Native American landholdings shrank from about 138 million acres to about 48 million acres.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that divided reservation land into plots for individual Native American families.

tossups.p: John Collier, Franklin Roosevelt’s Commissioner of Indian Affairs, pushed for a 1934 law that ended the policy begun by this earlier law. That 1934 law, the Indian Reorganization Act, encouraged Native nations to write constitutions and rebuild their own governments.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law, signed by Grover Cleveland, that broke up reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: In 1928, the Meriam Report described deep poverty on many reservations and criticized the land policy begun by this law. That report helped lead to a major change in federal policy toward Native Americans six years later.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that split up reservations into plots of up to 160 acres.

tossups.p: Reformers who called themselves “Friends of the Indian” and met each year at Lake Mohonk in New York backed this law. Helen Hunt Jackson’s book _A Century of Dishonor_ had earlier stirred calls to change the government’s treatment of Native peoples.
tossups.r: Supporters hoped this law would turn Native Americans into individual farmers. For 10 points, name this 1887 law that divided reservations into family plots.

tossups.p: This law gave 80 acres to each single adult and to each orphan under 18, and 40 acres to each other single person under 18. The federal government then sold off much of the reservation land left over after those plots were handed out.
tossups.r: Heads of families received 160 acres. For 10 points, name this 1887 law that broke up Native American reservations.

tossups.p: The federal government held each plot created by this law in trust for 25 years, and during that time the owner could not sell it. Native Americans who accepted plots under this law were also declared citizens of the United States.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that divided reservation land among individual Native American families.

tossups.p: The government labeled the reservation land it did not hand out under this law as “surplus” and opened it to white settlers. By the 1930s, Native nations had lost about two-thirds of the land they had held before this law passed.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law, signed by Grover Cleveland, that split reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: This law at first exempted the Cherokee, the Creek, and the rest of the “Five Civilized Tribes” in Indian Territory. Congress extended its policy to those nations with the Curtis Act of 1898, and a federal commission drew up membership rolls that those nations have used to decide citizenship.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that broke up Native American reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: Because land was sold to outsiders under this law, many reservations became a “checkerboard” of Native-owned and non-Native-owned plots. Over generations, the plots created by this law were divided among so many heirs that some owners held only tiny shares.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that split reservation land into plots for individual families.

tossups.p: This law gave each Native American head of a family the same amount of land that a settler could claim under the Homestead Act of 1862. Much of the land handed out under this law was too dry to farm, and many owners later lost their plots to taxes, debts, or fraud.
tossups.r: That amount was 160 acres. For 10 points, name this 1887 law that divided reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: The Massachusetts senator who sponsored this law chaired the Senate’s Committee on Indian Affairs. After leaving the Senate in 1893, he led a federal commission that pressed the “Five Civilized Tribes” to accept the policy of this law.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law, named for that senator, that broke up reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: The Burke Act of 1906 changed this law so that Native Americans who received plots became citizens only when the plot’s trust period ended, unless officials declared them “competent” sooner. Many owners who gained full control of their plots early soon lost them.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that split Native American reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: In 1903, the Kiowa leader Lone Wolf lost a Supreme Court case against the breakup of his people’s reservation under the policy of this law. In _Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock_, the Court ruled that Congress could override promises made in treaties.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law that divided reservations into plots for individual Native American families.

tossups.p: Native Americans who had not gained citizenship by accepting plots under this law were made citizens by the Indian Citizenship Act of 1924. A decade later, the Indian Reorganization Act stopped any further dividing of reservations under this law.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1887 law, signed by Grover Cleveland, that broke up reservations into individual plots.

tossups.p: This law was signed just four days after the Interstate Commerce Act, which created the first federal agency to regulate railroads. A former governor of New York signed both laws in February 1887.
tossups.r: That president was Grover Cleveland. For 10 points, name this law that aimed to turn Native Americans into individual farmers by dividing up reservations.

trap.title: Act, not Plan
trap.body: Several famous Daweses show up in history questions. Senator Henry Dawes of Massachusetts sponsored this 1887 law about Native American land, while Charles Dawes, a banker who later became Calvin Coolidge’s vice president, led the committee behind the 1924 Dawes Plan for Germany’s World War I reparations. William Dawes rode with Paul Revere in 1775. Saying “Dawes Plan” for this law is wrong, and so is the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934, which ended allotment.
trap.fix: Native American land, 160-acre plots, “surplus” land sold to settlers, and 1887 mean the Dawes Act; Germany, reparations, and the 1920s mean the Dawes Plan. “Dawes” or “General Allotment Act” is fine, but “allotment” alone may earn only a prompt.
trap.line: Real answer line: Dawes Act (or Dawes Severalty Act or General Allotment Act; prompt on allotment; do not accept “Dawes Plan”)
